frontier.hypothesis: A second use of the preheader copy destination that cse CANNOT fold to base would leave the surviving copy as a copy of the POINTER placed before the base add - the exact target shape - on the S2/V1 symmetric chassis where everything else already matches.
frontier.mechanism: Combine keeps a reg-reg move whose dest has 2+ uses (proved this session by V1 and Z1). Every second use tried so far was an address of the form sh + q + K, which cse recognises as base + K and folds, moving the surviving copy onto base and after the base add. A second use that reads the pointer through a DIFFERENT addend - the other slot's shift (slot_b << 6), a use in the loop body's early-return arm, or a use whose address the target also materialises independently - would not be foldable to base.
frontier.next_probe: On tmp/grind/func_80017848/s53/body_S2.c enumerate non-base-relative second uses of q and q2: (a) fold *(s32 *)((slot_b << 6) + (s32)q2 + 0x18) into the loop-2 guard test, (b) use q2 inside the do-while body's early-return arm, (c) pass q2 as math_Distance3D's SECOND (slot_b-shifted) argument, which the target computes from a separate sll. Measure each and diff the preheaders against s53/T.txt lines 34-37 and 58-61.

frontier.hypothesis: On the symmetric chassis the guard's pointer/shift seat swap (build a1/a0 vs target a0/a1) is a consequence of the missing copy, not an independent residual, so it will resolve for free once the copy lands.
frontier.mechanism: In S2 the pointer pseudo dies at the base add (REG_DEAD in .combine insn 89), which shortens its live range and changes its position in the allocation order; the target's copy extends the pointer's range by one insn. Loop-1's seats are already correct in BASE, where the pointer is live into loop 2's guard.
frontier.next_probe: Take the best cell that materialises a POINTER copy in a preheader (V1 for loop 1) and check whether that loop's guard seats are a0/a1 in tmp/grind/func_80017848/s53/B_V1.txt; if they are, the seat swap is dependent and needs no separate lever. Then re-measure S2 with only loop 1 chained to isolate.

frontier.hypothesis: Z1 (9 at 127/127) is a better starting chassis than BASE (3 at 127/127) for the remaining work even though its score is higher, because its residual is entirely preheader shape while BASE's 3 encodes the structural asymmetry.
frontier.mechanism: Score counts differing instructions, not distance-to-solution. BASE is 3 because its asymmetric spelling happens to land the loop-1 preheader and the loop-2 guard load in the right places, and that same spelling cannot also buy loop-2's copy (measured across s11-s52). Z1 has both loops in the target's structural shape with only the copy's kind and position wrong.
frontier.next_probe: Run the frontier-1 probes on the Z1 body (memory/grind/func_80017848/rejected/s53_chain_plus_loop2_latch_via_q2_BEST_M_BRANCH_costs_9.c) as well as on S2, and record BOTH scores per cell so the next session can see which chassis the lever moves.
